title: Dark-Mode Control of Contrasting Entanglement and Bell Nonlocality between Mechanical Oscillators
authors: Souvik Agasti, Philippe Djorwe, Xin Zhou
abstract: This study presents a detailed proposal for an optomechanical system consisting of two mechanical oscillators coupled to a common cavity, aimed at generating pure and entangled two-mode squeezed mechanical steady states. We found that the violation of Bell's measurement may not occur where the entanglement is maximum; rather, nonlocality can be observed for lower entangled states. A central result is that optomechanical coupling imperfections can enhance mechanical entanglement while simultaneously suppressing Bell nonlocality by reducing the purity of the mechanical state. To mitigate this trade-off, we introduce phase-dependent phonon hopping between the mechanical oscillators and show that Bell nonlocality can be selectively enhanced in specific dark-mode configurations, even when the overall entanglement is reduced. We trace this contrasting behaviorto changes in state purity associated with the imbalance of the Bogoliubov-mode occupations. Compatible with existing microwave cavity optomechanical platforms, the proposed architecture provides an experimentally accessible route for controlling nonlocal quantum correlations in multimode mechanical systems. Our proposed scheme serves as an attractive platform for the deployment of continuous-variable teleportation and high-fidelity quantum communication.
summary: This paper proposes using a coupled optomechanical system to control quantum correlations between mechanical oscillators. It reveals that entanglement and Bell nonlocality can behave oppositely when system imperfections are present. By introducing phase-dependent phonon hopping, the authors demonstrate a method to selectively boost Bell nonlocality for quantum communication applications.
main_problem: The study investigates the complex and often contrasting relationship between mechanical entanglement and Bell nonlocality in coupled optomechanical systems.
main_result: The authors show that coupling imperfections can enhance entanglement while suppressing Bell nonlocality, but phase-dependent phonon hopping allows for the selective enhancement of nonlocality even when entanglement is reduced.
method: The analysis uses theoretical modeling involving the derivation and solution of Quantum Langevin Equations (QLEs) in the resolved-sideband regime.
model_or_system: The system is an optomechanical setup comprising two mechanical oscillators coupled to a common cavity field. The dynamics are described by a Hamiltonian incorporating optomechanical, phonon-exchange, and driving terms.
key_observables: Entanglement (logarithmic negativity), CHSH Bell nonlocality, and state purity.
important_parameters: Coupling imperfections, phase-dependent hopping strength, and the operating regime (resolved-sideband).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the resolved-sideband regime (mechanical frequency much larger than cavity decay rate).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the system block diagram, boundaries for entanglement and nonlocality, and the dependence of Bell nonlocality on phase angle and coupling imperfections.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the Hamiltonian and system architecture to deriving the dynamics via QLEs, analyzing the impact of imperfections, and finally proposing phase-dependent hopping to selectively control nonlocality.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles the non-trivial interplay between different quantum correlation measures (entanglement vs. nonlocality) in a controllable, experimentally realizable platform (optomechanics).
